title: Regrouping a compact filtered presentation along a colimit-preserving functor
statement:
Use universes, smallness, regular cardinals, filteredness, compactness, coherent diagrams and colimits from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable regular cardinal in the smaller universe. Let $\mathcal E,\mathcal F$ be locally small infinity categories admitting all small colimits, and let $H:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ preserve all small colimits. Let $\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal F$ be a full subcategory closed under equivalence, consisting of $\kappa$-compact objects and closed under $\kappa$-small colimits computed in $\mathcal F$. Let $A$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered partially ordered set and $q:N(A)\to\mathcal E$ a diagram such that $q(a)$ and $H(q(a))$ are $\kappa$-compact for every $a\in A$. Write $x=\operatorname{colim}_{N(A)}q$. Suppose there is a small $\kappa$-filtered partially ordered set $J$ and a diagram $r:N(J)\to\mathcal P$ with $\operatorname{colim}_{N(J)}r\simeq H(x)$ in $\mathcal F$.

For each subset $b\subseteq A$ of cardinality less than $\kappa$ which is filtered in its inherited order (including nonemptiness), choose a colimiting cocone on $q|_{N(b)}$ with apex $x_b$. Let $B$ be the partially ordered set, ordered by inclusion, of those subsets $b$ for which $H(x_b)\in\mathcal P$. Then $B$ is small and $\kappa$-filtered, and every subset $T\subseteq A$ of cardinality less than $\kappa$ is contained in some $b\in B$. The chosen partial colimit cocones assemble to a coherent diagram $q':N(B)\to\mathcal E$, with $q'(b)=x_b$, and to a compatible colimiting cocone with apex $x$, whose components are induced by the original cocone on $q$. Every $q'(b)$ is $\kappa$-compact and $H(q'(b))\in\mathcal P$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.5.4.14 proof, printed p. 481, good partial-colimit construction using Lemma 5.5.4.13, Proposition 4.2.3.4 and Corollary 4.2.3.10; generic functor form of that construction.

proof.text: Fix a subset T of A with cardinality less than κ. Since H preserves all small colimits, the cocone Hq over A is colimiting with apex H(x); it is equivalent to the given colimit cocone for r over J. Apply the common-refinement lemma to the two κ-filtered posets A and J, the compact-valued diagrams H∘q and r, and the subsets T and the empty subset. It supplies filtered subsets b⊂A and c⊂J of cardinality less than κ, with T⊂b, and an equivalence between colim_{N(b)} Hq|_{N(b)} and colim_{N(c)} r|_{N(c)}.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 proof, printed p. 481: apply Lemma 5.5.4.13 to the presentation of H(x) and the prescribed P-presentation.

proof.text: The chosen cocone on q|_{N(b)} has apex x_b, and H preserves this colimit, so H(x_b) is equivalent to colim_{N(b)} Hq|_{N(b)}. Composing with the equivalence from the preceding step identifies H(x_b) with colim_{N(c)} r|_{N(c)}. This is a κ-small colimit: the nondegenerate simplices of N(c) are finite strict chains in c, so there are at most max(ℵ₀,|c|)<κ, using the uncountability of κ. Every value of r lies in P, and P is closed under κ-small colimits computed in F and under equivalence; hence H(x_b) belongs to P. Thus b is in B, and every T of cardinality less than κ is contained in an element of B.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 proof, printed p. 481: the good partial colimit has image in the closed compact subcategory.

proof.text: The collection of subsets of the small set A is small, so its subcollection B is small. Taking T to be the empty subset in the preceding construction shows that B is nonempty. This also records the required empty-subset convention for filteredness.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 proof, printed p. 481: smallness and the initial good partial colimit.

proof.text: Let (b_i)_{i∈I} be any family in B indexed by a set I of cardinality less than κ. Regularity of κ gives |⋃_{i∈I}b_i|<κ. Applying the containment property of Step 2 to T=⋃_{i∈I}b_i gives b∈B with ⋃_{i∈I}b_i⊂b, hence an upper bound for the family. For I empty this is the nonemptiness already proved. Therefore B is κ-filtered as a partially ordered set. Equivalently, any diagram from a κ-small simplicial set into N(B) uses fewer than κ vertices of B. An upper bound for those vertices extends the diagram to a cocone, since the order uniquely supplies all simplices involving the new final vertex. Thus N(B) satisfies the quasicategorical filteredness convention as well.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 proof, printed p. 481: regularity gives filteredness of the good-subset poset.

proof.text: For b∈B, the nondegenerate simplices of N(b) are finite strict chains in b. Their number is at most max(ℵ₀,|b|)<κ because κ is uncountable, so N(b) is κ-small. The diagram q|_{N(b)} has κ-compact values by hypothesis, E is locally small and admits all small κ-filtered colimits, and its chosen colimiting cocone has apex x_b. The compact-small-colimits lemma therefore shows that x_b is κ-compact.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 proof, printed p. 481: compactness of each good partial colimit.

proof.text: Regard N(b) as a simplicial subset of N(A). For each simplex of N(A), its finite set of vertices is contained in some b∈B by Step 2, and the whole simplex then lies in N(b), since b has its inherited order. Hence the subsets N(b) cover N(A), and inclusion b⊂b′ induces inclusion N(b)⊂N(b′). The index B is small, nonempty and directed by Steps 3 and 4. Apply the directed-cover colimit-assembly lemma to this cover, the diagram q, and the chosen colimiting cocones with apices x_b. It produces a coherent diagram q′:N(B)→E with q′(b)=x_b and a compatible colimiting cocone from q′ to x whose components are induced by the original cocone on q.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 proof, printed p. 481, using Proposition 4.2.3.4 and Corollary 4.2.3.10 for the coherent partial-colimit assembly.

proof.text: By Step 5 every object q′(b)=x_b is κ-compact, and by the definition of B every H(q′(b))=H(x_b) lies in P. Together with the coherent assembly and colimiting cocone from Step 6, these are all the asserted properties.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.14 proof, printed p. 481: final verification of the refined presentation.
